perspective:
Mason’s available information:

- I am Mason Hurley, an accountant at a small community center. Martha Moua is a personal care aide there; we are colleagues in a professional but not close relationship.
- I reviewed the community center’s financial reports and noticed discrepancies.
- I suspected Martha might be mismanaging funds, which made me suspicious and anxious.
- I asked Martha to discuss the recent financial report, saying the numbers did not add up.
- I told her the healthcare expenses seemed unusually high and did not align with usual spending patterns.
- I heard Martha say there was likely a reasonable explanation, that there might have been a misentry, and that she would review and correct any errors.
- After reviewing the report with Martha, I understood the discrepancies were due to a simple clerical error, not mismanagement. I felt relieved and embarrassed.
- I told Martha I appreciated her quick clarification and apologized for my initial suspicion and for not asking her first.
- I heard Martha say it was okay, that errors happen, that she understood I was being thorough, and that we should double-check entries next time.
- Later, I believed Martha was competent, but I believed the recurring clerical errors showed the financial management system was inadequate. I felt frustrated with the system but empathetic toward Martha.
- I discussed prevention with Martha, saying the issue was not her management but the current system.
- I proposed a new, more robust financial system and said I would draft a proposal and wanted her input.
- I heard Martha agree and offer to help make sure it addressed the gaps we identified.
- I drafted the proposal, felt hopeful it would benefit operations, but was uncertain whether management would approve and implement it.
- I told Martha about the draft and my uncertainty. She encouraged me to present it confidently and said the benefits were clear.
- I asked Martha to help gather data to strengthen our case, and she agreed.
- I prepared and presented the proposal to management.
- Afterward, I felt satisfied but physically and mentally exhausted, believing I had done everything possible.
- I told Martha the presentation went well and that it was now up to management.
- I heard Martha praise my work and suggest I take time off.
- I thanked her, planned to take a few days off to recharge and reflect, and hoped we would return to good news.
- I heard Martha wish me a good break and offer help while I was away.
